key_fields.sql: select z.borough, count(*) as touches from lake.trips t join ops.zones z on z.locationid = t.pulocationid or z.locationid = t.dolocationid group by z.borough order by z.borough
key_fields.claim: The BLOCKWISE_NL_JOIN is chosen because the OR predicate prevents hash join optimization; rewriting as a UNION ALL of two separate joins (one on PULocationID, one on DOLocationID) would enable hash joins and avoid the nested loop.

value.sql: WITH pu AS (SELECT z.Borough, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM lake.trips t JOIN ops.zones z ON z.LocationID = t.PULocationID GROUP BY z.Borough), do AS (SELECT z.Borough, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM lake.trips t JOIN ops.zones z ON z.LocationID = t.DOLocationID GROUP BY z.Borough), both AS (SELECT z.Borough, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM lake.trips t JOIN ops.zones z ON z.LocationID = t.PULocationID AND z.LocationID = t.DOLocationID GROUP BY z.Borough) SELECT coalesce(pu.Borough, do.Borough, both.Borough) AS Borough, (coalesce(pu.cnt, 0) + coalesce(do.cnt, 0) - coalesce(both.cnt, 0)) AS touches FROM pu FULL JOIN do ON pu.Borough = do.Borough FULL JOIN both ON coalesce(pu.Borough, do.Borough) = both.Borough ORDER BY Borough;
value.change_summary: Replaced the OR join with two separate equi-joins (PU and DO) plus an intersection join, aggregated each, then combined via full outer join using inclusion-exclusion to preserve exact per-borough counts.
value.risk_notes: None; inclusion-exclusion with full outer join guarantees row-equivalence because zones.LocationID is unique and every trip row contributes to PU, DO, or both without duplication.
